name: Git Helpers
description: Slash commands for everyday Git writing tasks: changelog, PR description, release notes, stand-up summary, and a conventional commit message.
author: TGGAGS

commands.name: changelog
commands.description: Write a changelog entry from recent commits
commands.template: Read the git log since the last tag (or the last 30 commits if there is no tag) and write a Keep-a-Changelog style entry grouped into Added / Changed / Fixed. Only describe things that really changed. $ARGUMENTS

commands.name: pr-description
commands.description: Draft a pull request title and description for the current branch
commands.template: Compare the current branch with its base branch (use git log and git diff against main/master or the upstream) and draft a pull-request title plus a description with Summary, Changes, Testing and Risks sections. Do not run git push. $ARGUMENTS

commands.name: release-notes
commands.template: Write friendly, user-facing release notes for the changes since the last release tag. Lead with the most important improvements, avoid internal jargon. $ARGUMENTS

commands.name: standup
commands.description: Summarise what I did recently from git history
commands.template: Summarise my git activity from the last working day (git log --author for the configured user.name) as a short stand-up update: Done / In progress / Blockers. $ARGUMENTS

commands.name: conventional-commit
commands.description: Write a Conventional Commits message for the staged changes
commands.template: Look at the staged changes (git diff --staged) and write a single Conventional Commits message (type(scope): subject, then a body if useful). Show it; do not commit. $ARGUMENTS
